name: Airbus A330-200
sources: [AC] Airbus A330 Aircraft Characteristics - Airport and Maintenance Planning, Rev 34, Dec 01/25 https://www.aircraft.airbus.com/sites/g/files/jlcbta126/files/2025-12/AC_A330_20251201.pdf: one document for the A330-200, -200F, -300, -800 and -900; p. is the PDF's page. General Aircraft Dimensions, A330-300 (fig 2-2-0-991-001, p.60, p.61) then A330-200 (fig 2-2-0-991-002, p.62 to p.64): overall length 63.67 m, 58.82 m (59.00 m with the first, taller fin, before Mod 48979); fuselage 62.89 m, 57.51 m; nose gear 6.67 m aft of the nose on both; main gear 32.05 m, 28.85 m; engine inlet 21.14 / 21.45 / 21.28 m, 17.94 / 18.25 / 18.08 m (GE / PW / RR); wing tip 39.1 to 42.22 m, 35.96 to 39.04 m; fin root leading edge 52.43 m, 47.09 m; tailplane tip 61.67 to 63.7 m, 56.36 to 58.37 m. On both: span 60.3 m, tailplane span 19.4 m, fuselage 5.64 m across, track 10.68 m.

Fuselage [AC]: no plug length is printed; the lengths come from the holds and the stations. Ahead of the wing, 3.20 m shorter: the forward cargo compartment is 11.82 m against 15.02 m (fig 2-6-1-991-003, p.104); the main gear (32.05 to 28.85 m) and the three engine inlets are each 3.20 m nearer the nose, the wheelbase is 22.180 m against 25.375 m (3.195 m; p.541, p.545), door 2 moves 3.18 m and door 3 3.19 m. The nose gear (6.67 m), door 1 (5.85 m) and the forward cargo door (9.53 m) do not move: the length comes out between the forward cargo door and door 2. Behind the wing, 2.13 m shorter: the aft cargo compartment is 10.19 m against 12.32 m, the bulk compartment 4.04 m on both (p.104); door 4 moves 5.33 m, the bulk cargo door 5.34 m, the fin root 5.34 m and the tailplane tip 5.31 to 5.33 m, each less the 3.20 m ahead of the wing. Door 3 moves with the wing only and the aft cargo door moves 5.38 m: the length comes out between door 3 and the aft cargo door.

Doors [AC] Door Location, fig 2-7-0-991-006 (p.119 A330-300 and -900, p.117 A330-200 and -800), centre lines from the nose, A330-300 then A330-200: door 1 5.85 m, 5.85 m; door 2 17.74 m, 14.56 m; door 3 35.96 m, 32.77 m; door 4 50.96 m, 45.63 m; forward cargo door 9.53 m, 9.53 m; aft cargo door 44.36 m, 38.98 m; bulk cargo door 47.35 m, 42.01 m. Four doors on each side on both, none added or left out: the base's doors moved with the fuselage (the tool puts them at 5.85, 14.54, 32.76 and 45.63 m). No stations of its own; the nose and the cockpit windows are the base's.

fore and aft (where the length comes out, metres aft of the base's nose on the base's mesh): the tool's own choice is the whole constant section each side of the wing, which puts door 2 at 15.76 m and door 3 at 32.01 m, 1.20 m and 0.76 m from their published places. On the A330-300 the forward length lies between the forward cargo door's aft edge (9.53 m + half of its 2.70 m, p.127: 10.88 m) and door 2's forward edge (17.74 m less half of its 1.07 m, p.124: 17.20 m). The aft length lies between the end of the wing-to-body fairing and the aft cargo door's forward edge (44.36 m less half of its 2.72 m, p.130: 43.00 m); the fairing ends about 38.9 m from the nose on the A330-300 and about 35.7 m on the A330-200 (measured on the side views of p.119 and p.117 at 300 dpi, 21 px/m): it stays with the wing. The base's mesh is 63.06 m long against the document's 63.67 m (x 0.990): the edges are at 10.78, 17.04 and 42.59 m on it, its fairing ends at 38.14 m and its tail starts to rise at 42.5 m. Taken a little inside: 10.9 to 16.9 m and 38.2 to 42.4 m.

The rest: foreM + aftM = -5.33 m is the fuselage (the side views give 62.89 - 57.51 = 5.38 m, the stations behind the wing 5.31 to 5.34 m). The overall lengths differ by less: 4.85 m (63.67 - 58.82), and 4.67 m with the first fin (59.00 m). The overall length is measured to the fin tip's trailing edge (52.43 + 8.14 + 3.1 = 63.67 m; 47.09 + 8.63 + 3.1 = 58.82 m; 47.09 + 9.12 + 2.79 = 59.00 m), and the A330-200's bigger fin reaches 1.31 m (1.49 m) behind the end of the fuselage against 0.78 m on the A330-300. The rest of 0.48 m (0.66 m) is the fin, which the model does not have. The model's fuselage, doors, gear and tailplane are where the A330-200 has them; by the document's measure it is 58.34 m long overall, 0.48 m less than the aircraft.

Fin: the A330-200's fin is taller than the A330-300's, and the tool keeps the base's fin. [AC] p.60, p.62, p.63: A330-300 8.3 m tall, root chord 7.79 m, tip chord 3.1 m; A330-200 9.3 m, 8.58 m and 2.79 m before Mod 48979, and 8.8 m, 8.58 m and 3.1 m after it (the 'shorter fin installation', p.74). Fin tip above the ground at maximum ramp weight, forward CG (Ground Clearances, p.73, p.74): 16.94 m on the A330-300; 17.98 m and 17.48 m on the A330-200. The model's fin is 0.5 m (1.0 m) too low and 0.79 m too short at its root.

The same on both aircraft, so the recipe has no wingtip, nacelle or gear. Wing [AC] p.60 to p.64: span 60.3 m with the same winglets, 10.56 m across the wing root, flap track fairings 7.46, 10.88, 14.21 and 17.65 m from the centre line; the wing tip is 3.14 to 3.18 m nearer the nose, as the wing is. Nacelles: one set of figures for the A330-200 and the A330-300 (2-12-0, p.204 to p.215: PW4000, Trent 700, GE CF6-80E1); nacelle above the ground 0.67 to 0.94 m on the A330-200 and 0.69 to 0.94 m on the A330-300 (p.74, p.73). Gear, Landing Gear Footprint (fig 7-2-0-991-003, p.541; fig 7-2-0-991-006, p.545): four wheels on each main leg and two on the nose leg, track 10.684 m, main wheels 1.397 m apart, axles 1.981 m apart, nose wheels 0.710 m apart, main tyres 1400x530R23 (or 54x21-23), nose tyres 1050x395R16, on both. Only the wheelbase differs: 22.180 m against 25.375 m; the tool takes the forward 3.20 m off the base's.

A338: the A330-800 is drawn on this model. It has the A330-200's fuselage, doors and gear: overall length 58.82 m, fuselage 57.51 m, main gear 28.85 m aft of the nose, the fin 8.80 m tall ([AC] fig 2-2-0-991-012, p.67); the door stations of p.117; wheelbase 22.180 m and the same tyre sizes (p.549). It differs from this model: span 64.00 m, with longer, curved wing tips in place of the winglets (p.67, p.68); Trent 7000 nacelles 3.71 m across against the Trent 700's 3.05 to 3.2 m, the inlet 17.86 m from the nose (p.217, p.209). This model shows it with the A330-200's wing tips and nacelles.

A332 is also the A330-200F's designator. The freighter has the same length, span and gear stations (58.82 m, 57.51 m, 60.3 m, 6.67 m and 28.85 m; [AC] fig 2-2-0-991-003, p.70), with one door on each side (5.85 m), a main deck cargo door behind the left one (9.92 m) and a few single windows in place of the window row (p.121). This model shows it with the passenger aircraft's doors and windows.
